item: decision J17. Rules whose best source is not stored: Keep them marked and in force; check each when the source is fetched (Nickerson 2013, Kundisch 2022, Cohen 1960, Berlin 1992, biology codes, *A Pattern Language*)

spec T6. Facets. Every facet value has a glossary entry; no value is empty in the latest classification (an empty cell asks whether a concept or an axis is wrong, Kwasnik pp.

process step 7. Classify fresh items, fix, repeat (who: model). Classify a fresh test sample using only `facets.md` and `glossary.md`. Note every hesitation; put items that fit no value in the facet's Unsorted list (S6).

spec T8. Agreement. Two raters classify the same fresh items independently, using only `facets.md` and `glossary.md`. Compute Cohen's kappa per facet. Target: κ ≥ 0.6 on every facet (J5). Disagreements show where the vocabulary is unclear (Z39.19 §11.2.2, pp.
scope.md field. Neighbours: other contexts it touches, and the map file
decision J7. Sample sizes: Build from 30-60 items, test on 30 fresh items per round; light version under ~30 items
spec T1. Integrity. Every ID unique; every record has all required fields; every referenced ID exists ("no cross-references ...
glossary.md field. Scope: what it includes and excludes, especially at the edges (D2)

spec S5. Add a level only when it says something new. A narrower term is added "only when there is something that we can say about this class that we cannot say about the superclass" (Noy and McGuinness §4.4).

process step 5. Test the bare facet list (who: model). Before writing any glossary entries, classify about 10 test items with the facet names and a one-line description of each value, and add, drop or split facets now.
decision J11. No evaluative words in names: Adopt as N7 (proposal 3)
scope.md field. Purpose: one sentence: what the taxonomy is for, and the one question every facet must help answer

spec G4. Named operations only. Every change is one of: add, rename (label changes, ID stays), split, merge, move (change broader or facet), redefine, deprecate. Each is logged in `changelog.md` and in the term's History with date and reason (Z39.19 §§11.3.1.2, 11.3.2.2, pp. 96-97).

spec D4. Near miss. One thing it is easily confused with, and why it is not it: the edge of the concept, where raters disagree. TnT-LLM's raters disagreed mostly at the boundaries between neighbouring labels (Wan et al. App.
glossary.md field. Broader: the ID of the nearest is-a parent (S5)

spec N2. Harvest, then choose. Collect the words already in use, with counts, before choosing. Choose the preferred label by warrant: the words in the content (literary warrant), the words of the readers (user warrant), and the owner's needs (organizational warrant) (Z39.19 §5.3.5).
decision J13. Find facets by comparison, and test the bare facet list early: Adopt both as process steps 4 and 5 (proposals 1 and 2)
glossary.md field. Example: a link to the clearest real case in the repo (D3)
process step 3. Harvest the words (who: model). List every term used for the things in the build sample, and in Jonathan's own words about the domain. Count each term's uses across the repo.

spec G1. Agents approve, Jonathan can veto. (J8, decided by Jonathan 2026-11-25). An agent may approve a change, or a term's move from `candidate` to `approved`, when every mechanical test (T1-T6) passes and the change is logged with its reason.

spec G5. Deprecate, never delete. A deprecated term keeps its record, ID, labels and history, and its Replaced by field names the term(s) to use instead; looking up an old label finds the deprecated record, which points on.
glossary.md field. Hidden: misspellings and old forms, kept for search, never shown as advice
decision J16. Replace "confidence" with a status: `candidate` / `approved` / `deprecated`
spec N1. One concept, one preferred name; one name, one concept. inside a context. Names must map to concepts one-to-one, with no homonyms and no synonyms (Deissenboeck and Pizka pp.
scope.md field. Competency questions: 5 to 15 questions the taxonomy must let you answer

spec T9. Guess the name. Show someone who has not seen the glossary a preferred label and ask what it means. A wrong guess means the name or the concept needs work (Meszaros and Doble, "Evocative Pattern Name").

process step 11. Put into use (who: model). Link `domains/<name>/glossary.md` in this repo from the domain repo's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` (by its GitHub URL) so agents there load it and use preferred labels (J2).

decision J8. Who has the final say: Agents approve, Jonathan can veto: an agent approves changes that pass T1-T6 with a logged reason; Jonathan is the named owner, reviews the changelog, can reverse anything and settles disputes
